ranking_note: Authored from the before description at origin/main commit a82eec4ded3a5b3d32ce7e2da62206df08331f14, frozen before any rewrite; protocol per /playbooks:skill-authoring ## Measurement. principles is the plugin's only skill, so every competitor lives in another plugin: testing:write writes tests, testing:test-value judges whether a test is worth keeping and whether to assert a mock call, testing:audit finds tests that cannot fail, testing:diagnose fixes failing tests, testing:plan finds coverage gaps in a diff, toolchain:check runs the build and tests, and mutation-testing:principles owns mutation-testing knowledge. Plugin eval loads only this plugin, so near-miss negatives test quietness, not competitor wins.

queries.request: My unit tests break every time I rename a private method, even though nothing a caller sees has changed. Why are they this fragile, and what principle am I breaking?
Is it worth replacing our Postgres repository with a fake in the order service tests, or should those tests hit the database? Explain the trade-off.
We're at 92% line coverage and management wants 100%. Is chasing that number a sensible goal for a test suite?
Explain the difference between the mockist and Detroit styles of unit testing, and which one leads to fewer brittle tests.
Our controller mixes HTTP parsing with the pricing rules and is miserable to test. How should I split it so the rules can be tested without starting the web host?
When I'm doing TDD, when should I hard-code the return value just to get to green, and when should I write the real implementation straight away?
What is the difference between a mock, a stub and a fake, and why does the distinction matter when designing tests?
I'm inheriting a ten-year-old billing module with no tests at all. Before I refactor it, how do I pin down what it does today so I can tell if I changed anything?
When does a rule that must hold for every input beat a handful of example tests, and how would I come up with good rules like that for a sort function?
Should my tests check the value a function returns, the state it leaves behind, or the calls it makes to its collaborators? Which is preferable, and why?
Write xUnit tests for the ShippingCostCalculator class in src/Shipping/ShippingCostCalculator.cs and put them in the right test project.
This test fails only on CI with a NullReferenceException in the fixture setup. Figure out why and fix it.
Scan the tests folder for tests that can never fail, such as ones with no assertions or ones that compare a value with itself.
Build the solution, run the test suite and the linter on the files I changed, and tell me whether anything breaks.
Here's the diff for the payments refactor. Which of the changed files need new tests, and where are the gaps?
Rename the variable orderTotal to grandTotal everywhere it appears in the repo.
Run Stryker on the pricing module and tell me which mutants survived and what that says about the suite.
What's the pytest flag to re-run only the tests that failed in the previous run?
This test asserts that calc.Add(2, 3) equals calc.Add(2, 3). Is it tautological, and where should its expected value come from instead?
Draft a short, friendly email to my landlord asking to renew the lease for another year.
